title: One reopen rule for a closed account (AP1, AR3, AO6): money out after the closing day, a check other than zero, a zero check, and an event on the closing day itself
story: Set up Mon 4 Jan 2027: the bank holds 300,000, of which Food 30,000 and Free to spend 50,000 (typed). Four e-wallets hold 10,000 each. Pay of 250,000 on the 25th (moved earlier). Wed 6 Jan: 2,000 of food paid with e-wallet 1. Fri 8 Jan the person pays 700 for lunch with e-wallet 1 at 09:00 and logs it on the phone at 21:00. At 10:00 the desktop closes all four e-wallets: each closing writes its final check (e-wallet 1 shows 7,300, the others 10,000) and moves the money to the bank (close:g1 to close:g4). Tue 12 Jan: a statement read for e-wallet 2 shows a 1,200 subscription still charged that day. Thu 14 Jan: a screenshot of e-wallet 3 shows 500 (a cashback came in), read as a check. Fri 15 Jan: a screenshot of e-wallet 4 shows 0, read as a check. Every amount is made up.

events.note: the closing moves the e-wallet's money out
lunch paid at 09:00, before the closing, logged at 21:00
a subscription the e-wallet still charged after it was closed
read from a screenshot: a check that reaches a closed account outside the check-in (AR3)
read from a screenshot: a zero check after the closing day

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 7,300 (the closing's final check, Fri 8 Jan 10:00: it holds everything dated on or before the closing day, so the lunch dated that day and logged at 21:00 is inside it [AP1]) - 7,300 (moved out by the closing, close:g1, which comes after its own check) = 0
asks.note: Before AP1 the lunch was judged by its told (AN4), came after the check, left -700 in a closed account and the model refused the copy [P6] (confirm_review_8 path a).

asks.question: warnings
asks.why: The lunch is dated on the closing day: it does not reopen e-wallet 1 [AO6, AP1]. Nothing else is dated after a closing day yet, and no account goes below its minimum.

asks.question: safe_to_spend
asks.why: 337,300 (bank today: 300,000 + 7,300 + 10,000 + 10,000 + 10,000 moved in by the four closings) - 27,300 (Food left this period: 30,000 less 2,000 and the 700 lunch, both spent on e-wallet 1 before it closed) = 310,000

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 0 (after the closing) - 1,200 (the subscription line dated Tue 12 Jan, after the closing day: it reopens e-wallet 2 [AP1]) = -1,200
asks.note: Before AP1 only money in reopened an account; money out left a closed account below zero and the model refused the copy (confirm_review_8 path d).

asks.question: warnings
asks.why: E-wallet 2 has a record dated after its closing day: it is open again, with a notice [AP1]. It is below zero, which is below its minimum of 0 [F9].

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 0 (after the closing) + 500 (the check dated Thu 14 Jan, a figure other than zero: it reopens e-wallet 3 and sets its bank figure [AO6, AP1, AR3]) = 500

asks.question: warnings
asks.why: E-wallet 3 is open again [AR3]. Its check shows 500 more than the app had (nothing), more than 20% of what it had, so the figure is asked about [O watch, X4]. E-wallet 2 is as before.

asks.question: warnings
asks.why: A zero check dated after the closing day does not reopen the account: AP1's "check" means a check with a figure other than zero [AV1, AO6]. E-wallet 4 stays closed, with no notice; e-wallets 2 and 3 are as before.

asks.question: bank_today
asks.why: 0 (closed, nothing in it) + 0 (the zero check of Fri 15 Jan, which reopens nothing [AV1]) = 0
